testHarnessContract.note: The package's own contract requires zero critical/serious axe violations, no touch target under 44px, and no horizontal overflow. The live per-tab a11y scan in A11Y_AUDIT.md found moneysweep-pr's shipped app violating all three of those requirements (color-contrast + button-name axe violations, 24px-tall tab triggers, mobile horizontal overflow) -- the app does not currently meet the bar its own design-system dependency sets for it.

importedSymbols.note: Counts are raw textual occurrences (import line + JSX usage) from a repo grep, not distinct call sites. All async/loading/empty/error UI is centralized in QueryBoundary.jsx and reused by ContractsTable, EntitiesTable, and RelationshipGraph. Roughly half of the package's exported surface is adopted; the badge variants for evidence tier / confidence / provenance / freshness / source, the icon button, and the whole theme-provider system are unused.

pilotTooling.role: moneysweep-pr's package.json carries three pilot-specific scripts on top of the usual dev/build/test scripts, indicating this repo was used as a design-package integration pilot rather than a plain consumer.

verify:federation-design.purpose: Asserts the installed @pr-federation/react package.json/lockfile resolution, downloads the pinned GitHub release tarball, and checks its sha256 against a hardcoded expected hash; also asserts shape of the package's release manifest, API snapshot (35 exports, 0 removed), design tokens (v2.0.0), and test-harness contract.

test:pilot.purpose: Node --test suite of static source-text assertions: verifies QueryBoundary wires every required shared async state, reacts to online/offline + stale-deadline events in the right branch order, that filterable views delegate to QueryBoundary instead of hand-rolling empty states, and that pilot components contain no hard-coded semantic Tailwind color utilities (forcing use of package tokens instead).

test:visual.purpose: Spawns its own Vite dev server on :4173, loads an isolated QueryBoundary fixture page (src/visual-tests/FederationPilotAtlas.jsx) at 6 viewports x 2 themes (light+dark, via a ?theme= query param), asserts every runtime state (loading/error/empty/filtered-empty/stale/offline incl. offline-precedes-loading and cached-data-visible-while-offline), runs axe + a 44px touch-target sweep + horizontal-overflow check per viewport/theme, and writes screenshots + a JSON report to docs/evidence/moneysweep-federation-design-pilot-v0-1/.
test:visual.reason: chromium.launch() in this script has no explicit executablePath and falls back to the default revision named in this repo's playwright-core 1.62.1 (chromium revision 1234). Only chromium revision 1194 is provisioned on disk in this environment (used by the shared a11y-runner via an explicit executablePath override). Running `npx playwright install` to fetch revision 1234 was explicitly out of scope for this audit, so the script was left failing with Playwright's own 'Executable doesn't exist' / run-install message rather than worked around. Its orphaned dev-server child process (spawned before the crash, on :4173) was found and killed as part of cleanup; no files were left behind by the aborted run.
test:visual.implication: The pilot's dedicated 6-viewport x 2-theme visual/axe/touch-target harness -- the most thorough check this repo owns -- is currently non-functional in a from-scratch environment because it doesn't pin its own browser executablePath the way the shared a11y-runner does. It could not be used to corroborate or refute this audit's findings; the live per-tab scan in A11Y_AUDIT.md is the only executed a11y evidence for this pass.

verify:pilot.purpose: Composite: runs verify:federation-design + test:pilot + lint + build.
verify:pilot.result: not run standalone (its components were run individually above; lint/build were out of scope for this audit)

shadcn.note: components/ui/button.jsx is generated and present but is not imported anywhere in src/ -- all real button surfaces in the app come from either FederationButton (via QueryBoundary) or bespoke raw <button> elements (ErrorBoundary.jsx, PageNotFound.jsx), never the shadcn primitive. components/ui/tabs.jsx (Radix Tabs) is the primary navigation control (grid-cols-6 TabsList) and is what overflows/overlaps at mobile width; see A11Y_AUDIT.md.

controlSourceMap.button: mixed: package FederationButton for QueryBoundary's retry/'Clear filters' actions; bespoke raw <button> in ErrorBoundary.jsx and lib/PageNotFound.jsx; local shadcn button.jsx exists but is unused
controlSourceMap.dialog: local-shadcn: Radix-based Sheet (components/ui/sheet.jsx) renders the Contract detail panel (ContractsTable.jsx) and Entity detail panel (EntitiesTable.jsx); the federation package has no dialog/sheet primitive
controlSourceMap.statusBadge: mixed: package FederationStatusBadge for contract/operational status in ContractsTable.jsx and StatsBar.jsx; local shadcn Badge for entity-type tags (EntitiesTable.jsx) and severity/ledger-state tags (GovernmentChanges.jsx) -- the package's own semantic/evidence/confidence/provenance badge variants are never used for these
controlSourceMap.emptyState: package: FederationEmptyState / FederationFilteredEmptyState / FederationOfflineState / FederationDegradedState / FederationStaleDataState / FederationErrorState / FederationLoadingState, all centralized through QueryBoundary.jsx and reused by every filterable tab
controlSourceMap.toggleControl: local (Radix Select via TypeFilterSelect.jsx -> components/ui/select.jsx), used for the Entities and Relationships type filters -- this is the control that fails axe's button-name check, see A11Y_AUDIT.md

themeSupport.note: The shipped app hardcodes document.documentElement.dataset.theme = 'dark' in main.jsx with no toggle control anywhere in the UI, and never imports FederationThemeProvider/useFederationTheme even though the package exports them. A separate, non-shipped fixture (src/visual-tests/FederationPilotAtlas.jsx, driven only by scripts/run-federation-pilot-visual-checks.mjs) does render both themes via a ?theme= query param for the pilot's own visual-regression checks, but it has no in-app entry point and is not part of the deployed dashboard, so 'light theme' is not reachable by an end user of this app.
